_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), Term II 2022, Series QQBRR/3 SET-1, Q.P. Code 31/3/1. 15 rendered pages (idx 0-14 = printed folios 1-15; the cover says 15 printed pages). idx 0 bilingual cover; ENGLISH on every EVEN index 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14; HINDI on every ODD index 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 (idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1-2, idx 3 Hindi Q3-6, idx 5 Hindi Q7-9, idx 7 Hindi Q10-12(a), idx 9 Hindi Q12(b)-13, idx 11 Hindi Section C + Q14, idx 13 Hindi Q15). Every odd page opens in Hindi: no English overflow onto any odd top. Last page idx 14 is English (Q15 only). The alternating hypothesis held with no parity inversion. Questions run 1-15 unbroken: idx 2 = instructions + Q1(a)/(b) + Q2; idx 4 = Q3, Q4(a)/(b), Q5, Q6(a)/(b); idx 6 = Q7, Section B header, Q8, Q9(a)/(b); idx 8 = Q10, Q11, Q12(a) + the OR; idx 10 = Q12(b), Q13; idx 12 = Section C note + Q14; idx 14 = Q15. STRUCTURE read off the printed English General Instructions (idx 2) and it matches term2_s10 exactly: (i) 15 questions, all compulsory; (iii) Section A Q1-7, 2 marks each; (iv) Section B Q8-13, 3 marks each; (v) Section C Q14 and 15 case-based, 4 marks each; (vi) internal choice in some questions, NO count printed. Section C's own note (idx 12): each case has sub-questions (a), (b), (c), with (a) and (b) compulsory and the internal choice in part (c). 14 + 18 + 8 = 40. INTERNAL CHOICE: the marking scheme (8 pages, every footer reads X_49_086_31/3/1, so this scheme is for set 31/3/1 alone, not merged with its siblings) prints a bare OR for Q1, Q4, Q6, Q9, Q12, Q14(c) and Q15(c), and for no other question; each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. 7 alternatives. No MCQs, so no answer key. Q7 part (c) is voided for half a mark by the scheme (printing error, 'green cells' for germ cells). Decimal points: the paper prints NO decimal number anywhere, so there is nothing to choose. No skip list (plan.txt: transcribe every question). 26 rows.

questions.stem:
Name the part/organ of the human female reproductive system

(a) where contraceptive devices such as loop or copper-T are placed to prevent pregnancy.

(b) which is blocked to prevent the transfer of eggs.

(d) from where the embryo gets nutrition from the mother’s blood.

In asexual reproduction, a single individual parent produces offsprings without the involvement of gametes. This method is a common means of increasing the offsprings rapidly under favourable conditions. Asexual reproduction occurs mostly in unicellular organisms, some plants and certain simple multicellular animals.
